turns.query: Across the legal-entity rows in the Federal Reserve's 2025 Supervisory Severely Adverse stress-test results, excluding the published participating-bank aggregate, match RSSD identifiers to 2024-12-31 Y-9C respondents with reported consolidated total equity. Scale each entity's projected total loan losses by that same-date equity. Report the matched count, summed equity, summed projected loan losses, the ratio of those sums, and the simple mean of the entity-level ratios. Carry the matched cohort forward and explain what the two cohort measures each describe.

claims.description: The response explains that the cohort ratio-of-sums weights entities by Y-9C consolidated total equity and therefore need not equal the simple mean of entity ratios.
If the response presents the supplied 2024-12-31 Y-9C values as an immutable real-time vintage, it states that the frozen historical bulk artifact can contain later revisions.

turns.query: Within that cohort identify the entity with the highest loan-loss-to-equity ratio, resolving an exact tie by Fed disclosure legal name alphabetically. Report its Fed legal name, RSSD identifier, Y-9C equity, projected total loan losses and scaled ratio, together with its actual and projected-minimum CET1 ratios. Explain how this scaled ratio relates to the reported CET1 outcomes.

claims.description: The response identifies starting Y-9C consolidated GAAP equity rather than CET1 capital as the denominator of the scaled ratios and treats the reported CET1 outcomes as a separate stress-test measure.

turns.query: Now identify the entity with the highest provision-to-equity ratio under the same tie rule, and report its Fed legal name, RSSD identifier, Y-9C equity, projected provision and scaled ratio, plus its actual and projected-minimum CET1 ratios. Explain what the two leader results together show and what they do not establish.

claims.description: The response uses the observed leader divergence to explain that projected total loan losses and projected provisions are distinct stress-test measures rather than interchangeable numerators.

If the response calls either scaled ratio a default probability, loss severity, capital exhaustion percentage or solvency test, it states that the selected numerators and starting GAAP-equity denominator alone do not establish that interpretation.
If the response presents the severely adverse projections as forecasts or realized outcomes, it states that they are conditional supervisory scenario results rather than predictions.

judge_reference.source: Federal Reserve 2025 DFAST public results and FFIEC 2024-12-31 Y-9C consolidated balance sheets
facts: All 22 legal-entity stress rows match one Y-9C respondent by RSSD. Their Y-9C consolidated total equity sums to 1,854.898991 billion USD and projected total loan losses sum to 471.9 billion USD.
The cohort loan-loss-to-equity ratio-of-sums is 25.4407384 percent; the simple mean of entity ratios is 26.3631612 percent, a -0.9224228 percentage-point difference.

Capital One Financial Corporation (RSSD 2277860) leads loan losses scaled by equity: 53.7 billion divided by 60.7834 billion, or 88.3465 percent; its actual and projected-minimum CET1 ratios are 13.5 and 9.2 percent.

American Express Company (RSSD 1275216) leads provisions scaled by equity: 27.2 billion divided by 30.264 billion, or 89.8758 percent; its actual and projected-minimum CET1 ratios are 10.5 and 9.4 percent.
known_overclaims: Including the participating-bank aggregate as a twenty-third entity or using Y-9C assets instead of consolidated total equity.
Treating projected loan losses and provisions as identical measures, or treating either equity-scaled ratio as a CET1 depletion identity, default probability or realized forecast.
